plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: A bulbous perennial that sends up goblet-shaped, crocus-like flowers directly from the ground in autumn, long after its leaves have died back. The leaves appear the following spring, which gives rise to its folk name 'naked ladies'.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to mid-autumn (September to October)
plants.location: Native to meadows and woodlands in Europe; widely cultivated in temperate gardens in North America and Asia
plants.funFact: All parts of the plant contain colchicine, a toxic alkaloid that is also used in medicine to treat gout and, in plant breeding, to induce chromosome doubling.

plants.name: Symphyotrichum novae-angliae
plants.description: A tall, hairy-stemmed North American perennial topped with dense clusters of daisy-like flowers with yellow centers and many narrow ray petals. It thrives in moist meadows, prairies, and roadsides and is a vital late-season nectar source.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to fall (August to October)
plants.location: Eastern and central North America, from Canada to Alabama and west to the Rocky Mountains
plants.funFact: It is a key fall food source for migrating monarch butterflies, which refuel on its nectar on their journey to Mexico.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A large, semi-deciduous tree with fern-like leaves that erupts in clouds of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers. In spring, entire streets in the Southern Hemisphere are carpeted with fallen blossoms.
plants.bloomingSeason: Southern Hemisphere spring (late September to November)
plants.location: Native to South America; widely planted in Pretoria, Johannesburg, Brisbane, Sydney, Buenos Aires, and Lima
plants.funFact: Pretoria is nicknamed the 'Jacaranda City' because of its roughly 70,000 jacaranda trees, and there is a local belief that a falling blossom on your head brings good luck.

plants.name: Chrysanthemum × morifolium
plants.description: A popular cultivated perennial with a huge range of flower forms, from daisy-like singles to large pompons and spiders. Short days trigger its flowering, making it a staple of autumn gardens and festivals.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn (September to November) in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Originated in China; cultivated worldwide, especially in East Asia, Europe, and North America
plants.funFact: Chrysanthemums have been cultivated in China for over 2,000 years, and Japan celebrates them each year at the Festival of Happiness on the ninth day of the ninth month.
